title: National reach network: ~100 big rivers have broken downstream links (lakes, tile edges)

title: 2. NASA IMERG Early/Late/Final ingestion
description: NASA GPM IMERG V07 half-hourly 0.1° grids (cell centres x.x5°; GES DISC products GPM_3IMERGHHE Early, GPM_3IMERGHHL Late, GPM_3IMERGHH Final), each pair of half-hours summed to an hourly total (precipitation is a mm/h rate per half-hour: depth = rate x 0.5 h). Early (about 4 h latency) fills the most recent hours; Late (about 14 h) overwrites Early for the same hour; Final (about 3.5 months) overwrites Late for history. Record the run per hour. Replaces JAXA GSMaP (decided 2026-11-19): rename the GSMAP_NOW/GSMAP_NRT product tags, the gsmap grid spec and weights_gsmap.npz to IMERG (same x.x5° alignment; check longitude convention -180..180 vs 0..360). Access: NASA Earthdata login; request an Earthdata bearer token for gpm1.gesdisc.eosdis.nasa.gov through the environment's credential flow (never in files or commits).
notes: Deferred 2026-11-19 (Sean): ECMWF + council gauges first. Revisit if the West Coast storm validation (rf-t26.7, one-off IMERG Final comparison) shows IMERG beats ECMWF against the gauges. Reasons: Early runs ~4 h late (newest hours come from ECMWF anyway); satellite estimates tend to undercount heavy orographic rain in the Southern Alps; gauge scaling does most of the correcting; Earthdata account/token, network allowance and ~200 MB/day to maintain.

title: 1. RainfallSource interface + rolling buffer + catchment weight matrix

Build once: sparse matrix grid cell (0.1°) -> catchment, weighted by the share of each cell's area inside the catchment (the national reach/local-catchment network). Every hour: one sparse mat-vec gives mm per catchment; x catchment area gives m³. Each slot keeps raw, scaled, factor, factor version and product.

ECMWF 0p1 precip is 3-hourly to 144 h: child 3 splits into hours.

title: Rainfall accumulation per catchment (IMERG + ECMWF, gauge-scaled)
description:
GOAL
For every catchment nationwide, keep a running total of rainfall (mm and m³) over the past x hours. x is any whole hour from 1 to 24; default windows are 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24h. Totals add up down the river network, so each catchment includes everything upstream.

SOURCES (all behind one RainfallSource interface; record which source supplied each hour)
1. NASA GPM IMERG (main source for observed rain; replaces JAXA GSMaP, decided 2026-11-19; free NASA Earthdata login)
   - Half-hourly 0.1° grids (V07, cell centres on x.x5°), summed in pairs into hourly totals.
   - IMERG Early Run (about 4 h latency) for the most recent hours; IMERG Late Run (about 14 h) overwrites Early for the same hour when it lands; IMERG Final Run (about 3.5 months, gauge-calibrated) overwrites Late when it exists (history and validation).
   - The newest ~4 h have no IMERG yet: ECMWF short-lead hours cover them (see 2a), with the product recorded per hour.
2. ECMWF IFS open data (first-class source, not a fallback)
   - 0.1° grid, published since 20 Oct 2026; one forecast run every 6 hours.
   - Two uses: (a) an alternative observed-window source built from the first few forecast hours of each run (the short-lead hours), so it can be compared with IMERG side by side; (b) a forecast metric: rain expected in the NEXT x hours.
   - Check the time step of the precipitation fields. If they come in 3-hourly steps, either split them into hours (and document how) or read the hourly ecmwf_ifs data from the Open-Meteo S3 bucket (s3://openmeteo, CC-BY 4.0).
   - Which source each metric uses is set in config, so either can be the main source for observed rain.

GAUGE COMPARISON + SCALING
- Read hourly rain-gauge data from regional council Hilltop servers. Start with West Coast, Canterbury and Tasman.
- For each source, compare grid totals with gauge totals per region over a rolling 30-day window, and compute a scale factor.
- Guard rails: a minimum-rainfall threshold before computing a ratio, limits on how far a factor can move, and a minimum number of gauges. With too few gauges, use factor = 1.0.
- Calculate factors separately for IMERG and for ECMWF.
- Store with every hourly slot: the raw value, the scaled value, the factor, and the factor version.

DOCUMENTATION (required)
- docs/rainfall-scaling.md: the method, regions, thresholds, limits, update schedule, and how a factor is traced back to the gauges and dates it came from.
- A table of the factors in use, plus a history of changes to them.
- A validation report for one past West Coast storm: catchment totals from IMERG and ECMWF against gauges, before and after scaling.

PIPELINE
- Build once: a sparse matrix of grid cell -> catchment, weighted by the share of each cell's area inside the catchment.
- Every hour: one matrix multiplication gives mm per catchment; multiply by catchment area to get m³.
- Keep the last 24 hourly values per catchment in a rolling buffer; any window is the sum of the last x values.
- Add totals down the network, working from upstream catchments to downstream ones, so each catchment includes everything upstream.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Any x from 1 to 24 can be configured; the defaults work as listed.
- Both sources run through the same interface and can be switched in config.
- Each hour shows which product it came from (IMERG Early / Late / Final, or ECMWF), and a later IMERG run overwrites an earlier one for the same hour (Late over Early, Final over Late).
- Scaling runs with its guard rails; raw and scaled values are both kept.
- The scaling documentation and the storm validation report are committed.
- The ECMWF forecast metric for the next x hours is available.

ACCESS NEEDED (check before starting each child)
- IMERG needs a NASA Earthdata login (Sean registers; an Earthdata bearer token goes only through the environment's credential flow for the GES DISC host, never in files or commits).
- Network hosts to allow as needed: NASA GES DISC (gpm1.gesdisc.eosdis.nasa.gov, plus urs.earthdata.nasa.gov if the token flow needs it), ECMWF open data (data.ecmwf.int) or the Open-Meteo S3 bucket, and the council Hilltop servers (West Coast, Canterbury, Tasman).
notes:
Access check 2026-11-19 from the cloud session: REACHABLE ecmwf-forecasts S3 (ECMWF open data mirror, s3://ecmwf-forecasts, eu-central-1) and Open-Meteo S3 (s3://openmeteo, data/ecmwf_ifs/*.om). BLOCKED by the environment's network policy: data.ecmwf.int, JAXA (hokusai.eorc.jaxa.jp, sharaku.eorc.jaxa.jp), council Hilltop hosts tried (hilltop.wcrc.govt.nz, data.ecan.govt.nz, envdata.tasman.govt.nz; exact Hilltop hostnames still to confirm). GSMaP is distributed over FTP/SFTP (hokusai), which the HTTPS-only egress proxy may not carry even if allowed: confirm an HTTPS route or run GSMaP ingestion elsewhere. Needs Sean: JAXA account, and approving the Hilltop hosts once confirmed.
2026-11-19: source switched from JAXA GSMaP to NASA GPM IMERG (Sean). Access check: gpm1.gesdisc.eosdis.nasa.gov, urs.earthdata.nasa.gov, jsimpsonhttps/arthurhouhttps.pps.eosdis.nasa.gov all blocked by the network policy; IMERG is HTTPS (unlike GSMaP FTP), so allowing the GES DISC host plus an Earthdata bearer token via the credential flow should work.
2026-11-19: IMERG ingestion deferred (rf-t26.2); ECMWF is the main observed source (config/rainfall.toml observed.source = ecmwf). Scaling, live publishing and the map layer proceed with ECMWF only.

title: Retrain the model on the river-guide research data, with switchable model versions
description:
Source: Sean's research agent output (river sections, gradients, etc.): https://claude.ai/public/artifacts/30f8fe9a-674f-4487-9665-9ad5c52b09fe . The page renders its data with JavaScript, so it cannot be fetched from the container: save the JSON into labels/ (e.g. labels/guide_research.json) first, then write an importer to labels.Section (river, section, region, grade, put-in/take-out, gradient, length, status, source, coordinate provenance).

Requirements (from Sean):
1. Checkpoint the current weights before retraining: freeze today's model (reference rivers only) as models/v1 (coef, intercept, mean/std, run params, label set, date) and never overwrite it.
2. Model registry: every trained model saved as its own versioned file (v1 = current, v2 = research data, room for future ones, e.g. XGBoost). Store per-segment scores per model, not just the latest.
3. Browser: a model picker in the viewer that switches scores, runs, candidate list and the 3D separation view between models (old vs new vs future) so they can be compared by feel. Remember the choice in the URL hash.
4. Coordinates: train and evaluate twice, with and without sections whose put-in/take-out coordinates were inferred (not sourced). Report both.
5. Train/test split: hold out whole rivers (not segments) so a river is never in both sets; stratify by region and grade. Keep the Mangakarengorengo held out. Fixed seed, split saved to the repo.
6. Model performance page in the web viewer: per model and per variant (with/without inferred coordinates): test ROC AUC, precision/recall at the run threshold, rank percentile of each test river, per-region results, coefficients, and a plain-language explanation of how to read them.
7. Top-runs list: label every run as 'Training river' (its segments were used to fit the current model), 'Test river' (held out, a real check), or 'Prediction' (not labelled at all). The label must follow the selected model.
8. Mark guide-listed sections from the research data as known runs (exclude them from candidates, show them as listed).
